site_cli.cert.le: Certificate: Let’s Encrypt{staging}, valid until {until} ({days} d left), issuer {issuer}
site_cli.cert.selfsigned: Certificate: the server’s self-signed one (valid until {until})
site_cli.check.head: Site check: {verdict}.
site_cli.check.verdict.dns_mismatch: DNS doesn’t match the server address
site_cli.check.verdict.http_error: the page or the redirect doesn’t respond
site_cli.check.verdict.panel_unreachable: the panel doesn’t respond at the secret path
site_cli.dns.state.elsewhere: the A records don’t point to this server
site_cli.dns.state.ok: all A records point to this server
site_cli.dns.state.partial: some A records point to other addresses
site_cli.domain.cleared: Domain removed: the panel, personal pages and inbounds are on the server’s self-signed certificate.
site_cli.domain.kept: The Let’s Encrypt certificate stays in {paths} (not renewed).
site_cli.domain.set: Domain {domain} set. The certificate isn’t issued yet: kaskadctl site cert issue
site_cli.email.email_or_clear: either an email or --clear, not both
site_cli.help.check: check the site, panel, redirect and certificate
site_cli.help.dns_wait: wait up to N seconds until ready (≤ 300)
site_cli.help.domain: set the domain or remove it (--clear); the working domain changes only after the new one is checked and gets its certificate
site_cli.help.email: email for Let’s Encrypt (no argument: show it)
site_cli.help.installed: hand the certificate over to its users (deploy hook)
site_cli.help.issue: issue (a valid one is not reissued)
site_cli.help.mode: domain or site mode (nginx and the site on 443)
site_cli.help.mode_random: a new random template (without the flag — the previous template if there was a site, else a random one)
site_cli.help.panel_path: secret panel path on the site
site_cli.help.panel_path_rotate: replace the path now; the old one becomes 404
site_cli.help.panel_url: panel address on the site (the path is hidden without --show)
site_cli.help.remove: remove the domain and Kaskad’s files for it
site_cli.help.site: domain, DNS and Let’s Encrypt certificate
site_cli.help.staging: Let’s Encrypt staging (for a test bench)
site_cli.help.tick_quiet: stay silent when all is well
site_cli.help.use: SSTP or OpenConnect on the domain certificate
site_cli.help.vhost: the site vhost by this version’s template (no flag: only check whether it is current)
site_cli.help.vhost_refresh: rewrite the vhost with the current settings; nginx -t, the previous file back on an error
site_cli.installed.done: Certificate handed over to its users: {names}.
site_cli.installed.lineage: This certificate is for another name — Kaskad leaves it alone.
site_cli.installed.no_domain: No domain set — nothing to hand over.
site_cli.issue.set_email: Set an email: kaskadctl site email <email>
site_cli.mode.off: Site turned off; the domain and certificate stay in domain mode.
site_cli.mode.on: Site turned on for the domain. Template: {name}.
site_cli.mode.vless_tls: TLS with its own domain, port 443
site_cli.onoff.bad: the value must be on or off, not {value}
site_cli.p443.behind: Port 443/tcp: held by the gateway’s xray (VLESS + TLS), the site works behind it.
site_cli.p443.busy: Port 443/tcp for the site: in use — {who}
site_cli.p443.not_behind: Port 443/tcp: held by the gateway’s xray, but the site is not behind it — the site won’t open on the domain: kaskadctl gw vless sync
site_cli.p443.orphan: Port 443/tcp: nobody listens — the site waits behind the gateway’s xray, but xray doesn’t hold 443/tcp; the site won’t open on the domain: kaskadctl gw vless sync
site_cli.p443.site: Port 443/tcp: the site is on it (nginx).
site_cli.p443.xray: Port 443/tcp: held by the gateway’s xray (VLESS); once turned on, the site goes behind it.
site_cli.remove.done: Domain and certificate removed from Kaskad.
site_cli.renew.not_due: Not due for renewal yet — certbot changed nothing.
site_cli.status.back: New settings needed when going back to self-signed: {list}
site_cli.status.certbot_no: no (installed when the certificate is issued)
site_cli.status.no_domain: Domain: not set (everything is on the server’s self-signed certificate). Set: kaskadctl site domain <name>
site_cli.status.pending: New settings needed when moving to the domain: {list}
site_cli.status.use: Domain certificate used by: panel — {panel}, personal pages — {pages}, SSTP — {sstp}, OpenConnect — {ocserv}
site_cli.tick.installed: The new certificate is handed over to its users.
site_cli.tick.missing: The certificate files are missing — issue it again.
site_cli.tick.none: No Let’s Encrypt certificate — nothing to watch.
site_cli.use.dry_off: Dry run: {title} would leave the domain certificate; devices that will need new settings: {n}.
site_cli.use.dry_on: Dry run: {title} would move to the domain certificate; devices that will need new settings: {n}.
site_cli.vhost.current: The nginx settings of the site are of this version.
site_cli.vhost.foreign: The nginx settings of the site are for another domain or panel path (are they being changed?) — left as they are.
site_cli.vhost.none: There is no site on the domain — nothing to rewrite.
site_cli.vhost.outdated: The nginx settings of the site are of an earlier version: kaskadctl site vhost --refresh.
site_cli.vhost.refreshed: The nginx settings of the site are updated and nginx has reloaded them.
site_cli.vhost.unchanged: The nginx settings of the site are already of this version — nothing changed.
site_cli.vhost.written_stopped: The nginx settings of the site are written; nginx is stopped — it reads them when it starts.
site_cli.help.vless_yes: agree to the price: the VLESS links change, give them to the devices again (without the flag, with VLESS devices — a refusal with the price)
site_cli.help.vless_site: the Reality cover site when the site goes off and none is kept (from gw vless masks --check)
